groups.hint: Think of how you'd answer 'How are things going?'
groups.explanation: These four words all describe the current standing or circumstances of something, as in 'in good ___'.

redHerrings.why: It can suggest a position or standing, but here it means to put up with something.

groups.hint: What you do with something unpleasant you can't avoid.
groups.explanation: Each word means to endure or put up with something, as in 'I can't ___ it'.

redHerrings.why: It also looks like an online name, which tempts a link to the shortened-word group.

groups.hint: Ways to make a word or name take up less room.
groups.explanation: Each is a way words commonly get shortened: dropping letters, merging words with an apostrophe, omitting sounds, or a short familiar name.

redHerrings.why: It can be abbreviated, but it belongs with the words about circumstances.

groups.category: WORDS MADE USING U.S. POSTAL ABBREVIATIONS
groups.hint: Look for the map hiding inside the spelling.
groups.explanation: Each word can be split entirely into two-letter U.S. state codes: CA-LA-MA-RI, MA-ND-AR-IN, ME-LA-MI-NE, AL-KY-LA-MI-DE.

redHerrings.why: It points straight at U.S. states, but it is not built from postal codes.
